page: Amazon Web Services r4.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is configured with two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 15.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.62 GB per core. It contains no onboard local storage, relying exclusively on network-attached volumes, includes no GPU hardware, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation.

Benchmark testing positions the r4.large within the lower relative performance tiers across computational and memory throughput metrics. In raw CPU assessments, it recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 846.0, a multi-core score of 980.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 1583.62. Memory throughput for uncached large blocks registered at 8.31 GB/sec for read operations and 5.85 GB/sec for write operations, corresponding to a PassMark memory score of 1499.05. Application-level tests reflect these hardware limits, yielding 0.62 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.52 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio, r4.large is suited for memory-weighted workloads that demand minimal processing capability, such as lightweight in-memory key-value caching, development or staging database instances, and modest batch workers. The primary architectural tradeoff is its legacy Broadwell processor family and lack of AVX-512 support, leading to lower per-core compute efficiency compared to modern alternatives.
description: Amazon Web Services r4.large is a memory-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor, powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. It provides 2 vCPUs across a single physical core, paired with 15.0 GB of RAM, offering a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.62 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage or GPU accelerators and provides a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. Supported instructions include AVX, AES, and FMA, though newer extensions like AVX-512 are absent. Across benchmarks, the legacy microarchitecture achieves modest results, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 980.0, a PassMark CPU score of 1583.62, and Redis SET throughput of 0.62 million operations per second. With large uncached read bandwidth of 8.31 GB/sec, the r4.large is positioned for memory-reliant workloads with low computational intensity, such as small-scale in-memory caches, development databases, and routine background jobs.
